Team —

Attached is the first draft of the Q3 OKR runway and the proposed escalation matrix for stakeholder sign-off. High-level asks here:

- Read the OKR runway doc (link + attachment) and flag any objective/metric that looks infeasible given current capacity.
- Review the escalation matrix: tiers, SLAs, and who owns the on-call escalation for customer-impacting regressions.
- RSVP for a QBR dry-run slot next week (proposed windows below). we need at least one exec + two owners in the dry-run.

Proposed dry-run windows (PDT):
- Tue 2027-05-11 10:00–11:30
- Wed 2027-05-12 14:00–15:30
- Thu 2027-05-13 09:00–10:30

Links & attachments:
- Draft OKR runway: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aQ3-OKR-runway-draft (doc)
- Attachments: Q3_OKR_runway_v1.docx (doc), escalation_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Key notes in the doc:
- We propose a -3% latency SLO target improvement on our hosted API for tier-1 routes, measured vs baseline of March 2027.
- Cost-efficiency target: 6% token-cost reduction via batching/quantization recommendations in Optimize.
- Escalation matrix favors automated rollbacks for model-regression events; human approval required for SLA exceptions.

Please reply with redlines by EOD Friday (2027-05-07). I will aggregate comments and circulate a consolidated sign-off list.

Thanks —
Mateo

Thanks Mateo — quick read-through. A few inline notes below (high level):

- Objective A (Latency SLO): tighten measurement window to 95th->99th pctl for external-facing routes; 95th alone masks tail spikes. If we commit to -3% at 99th, engineering capacity needs to be confirmed.
- Cost-efficiency target: the current quantization recommendation looks aggressive for small-batch latency; propose we pilot on non-critical routes first.
- Escalation matrix: add an explicit clause for data-retention queries (30-day evidence window). I will loop Security for a short check — I can coordinate that.

I can present the escalation slide during the dry-run if needed (happy to own it). For dry-run windows, Wed 2027-05-12 14:00–15:30 works best for me.

Kimberly Park
VP, Product Strategy | Redwood Inference
